title: Spanish present tense (regular verbs)
examples: How do I say 'we speak' in Spanish?
What are the endings for -er verbs?
Can you show me how to conjugate 'comer'?

explain.say: Today we learn to talk about actions happening now in Spanish.
First we look at verbs ending in -ar like hablar which means to speak.
Next we study verbs ending in -er like comer which means to eat.
Finally we look at verbs ending in -ir like vivir which means to live.
For example if you want to say 'We live' you use nosotros and the ending -imos.
In real life you use this when describing what you are doing right now.

faq.q: Do I use different endings for 'you' depending on where I am?
faq.a: Yes, there are different forms for 'you' depending on the region. In some places, they use 'vosotros' for all students.

faq.q: What is the base for the verb when I conjugate it?
faq.a: You remove the ending -ar, -er, or -ir to find the root. Then you add the correct ending.
asks: How do I find the root verb?
Do I change the root when I conjugate?

faq.q: Can I mix up the endings for -er and -ar verbs?
faq.a: It is easy to mix them up because the patterns look similar. Remember that -ar verbs use 'as' for tú.
asks: What is the difference between -ar and -er endings?
Which ending goes with 'tú' for -er verbs?

faq.q: Does 'Usted' mean you or a specific person?
faq.a: Usted is a formal way to say you to an adult or person you do not know well. It shows respect.
asks: When should I use Usted instead of tú?
Is Usted only for older people?

faq.q: What about irregular verbs like 'ser' or 'ir'?
faq.a: This lesson only covers regular verbs. Irregular verbs follow different rules and need to be learned separately.
asks: Are there any exceptions to these rules?
What is the first thing I should learn after this?

facts: Regular verbs in Spanish follow predictable patterns for conjugation.
The subject pronoun 'Yo' always means 'I' no matter the verb.
The endings change based on whether the verb ends in -ar, -er, or -ir.
Nosotros/as is the form used for 'we' in Spanish.

quiz.say: If the verb is 'comer' and the subject is 'Nosotros', what is the correct form?
quiz.why: For -er verbs, the 'we' form always ends in -emos.

wrong.0: This ending belongs to the -ar verb group.
wrong.1: This ending is for 'you all' in Spain, vosotros.
wrong.2: This ending is used for the third person singular, él/ella.

quiz.say: Which ending do I use for 'Él' when conjugating a verb like vivir?
quiz.why: For all three types of regular verbs, the third person singular uses the ending -e.

wrong.2: This ending is used for the -ar verbs.
